_Author: Tessa Forth (GEO-712)_

**This vignette explains how the ```biomassrecovery``` package works. In a nutshell, it reports tropical forest biomass recovery trajectories at the ecoregion scale.**

## Context

This package and repository were created as part of GEOG712: Reproducible Workflow in GitHub and R. The contents and function are adapted from my MSc thesis project, tentatively titled: “Evaluating the variability of tropical forest biomass recovery through a space-for-time synthesis of remote sensing datasets.”

_Note that there are two somewhat unrelated functions: ```multiplyr``` and ```fourthpowerr```. These were created as practice for navigating function-writing and package design. The following information details the “heart” of the package: tropical forest biomass recovery._

## Data Sources/Preprocessing

This package uses a preliminary export file called ```EcoregionExports.csv```. This is a CSV table that has pre-processed some ecoregion-level data on tropical forest biomass recovery rates, regression statistics, and nearby primary forest reference biomass. This data is derived primarily from the following sources:

- RESOLVE Ecoregions ([Dinerstein et al., 2017](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=37ea320eebb647c6838c23f72abae5ef#overview)).
- GEDI L4A Aboveground Biomass Density, Version 2.1 ([Dubayah et al., 2020](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/LARSE_GEDI_GEDI04_A_002?_gl=1\emph{1sanpqq}_up\emph{MQ..}_ga_ga_SM8HXJ53K2*czE3ODk2NzEyMTEkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODk2NzEyMTEkajYwJGwwJGgw)).
- GLAD Global Forest Change ([Hansen et al., 2013](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/UMD_hansen_global_forest_change_2025_v1_13)).
- JRC Tropical Moist Forests Annual Change Collection ([Vancutsem et al., 2021](https://forobs.jrc.ec.europa.eu/TMF/data)).

These data were produced through the following steps:

- In Google Earth Engine, 2020 GEDI footprints were sampled within primary forests and post-disturbance/regrowing forests within one ecoregion (excluding areas with anthropogenic influence).
  - Code links:
    - [Primary Forests](https://code.earthengine.google.com/273fa38c7dc60c3177209be042062c8b)
    - [Global Forest Change](https://code.earthengine.google.com/e347588e7711b4de0272882004d4b8bc)
    - [Tropical Moist Forests](https://code.earthengine.google.com/84d2db2b969db7ccb15e32307b2c21cc)
- In Google Colab, data on aboveground biomass were aggregated to the median within primary forests, as well as the median per year of regrowth - then, the relationship between biomass and age was modelled via linear regression and compared to the primary forest benchmark.

These steps resulted in the first-pass table of ecoregion results, ```EcoregionExports.csv```. Yet not all the data is fit for reporting yet, and there remain some critical variables to calculate.

## Package Functionality

This package reads the exported table, omits unnecessary data columns, and filters for records where ecoregion-level results were viable for reporting. It then calculates additional fields for reporting the “best” results.

To start with this package, you first need to set your environment up and read the CSV file.

```{r setup}
# Setup
#install.packages(“here”)
library(here)
library(biomassrecovery)

## Set file path
filepath <- here("data-raw", "EcoregionExports.csv")

## Read CSV file
df_ecoregions_original <- read.csv(filepath) # Storing this as its own object in Environment for reference
```

Then, we filter the data, starting by removing unnecessary columns for the Global Forest Change dataset, which will not make it to the final analysis.

```{r filtering_gfcremoval}
df_ecoregions <- subset(df_ecoregions_original,
                        select = -c(gfc_n, gfc_slope, gfc_int, gfc_r2))
```

Next, we want there to be no missing data, no negative growth slope and no excessively small R^2 values.

```{r filtering_cleanup}
### Remove records where ecoregions had no viable data points within Primary Forests or TMF Regrowing Forests
df_ecoregions <- df_ecoregions[df_ecoregions$pri_n != -1 & # -1: nodata flag
                               df_ecoregions$tmf_n != -1,]
### Ensure that only records with positive, nonzero slopes are kept
df_ecoregions <- df_ecoregions[df_ecoregions$tmf_slope > 0,]
### Remove ecoregions where R^2 was particularly low, less than 0.3
df_ecoregions <- df_ecoregions[df_ecoregions$tmf_r2 >= 0.3,]
```

Then, we calculate new fields for comparing the biomass recovery trajectories to the benchmark of primary, old-growth forest levels of biomass.

```{r newreports}
## Calculate the predicted biomass after 20 years of regrowth (via linear regression)
df_ecoregions$tmf_agbd20 <- df_ecoregions$tmf_slope * 20 + df_ecoregions$tmf_int

## Calculate the percent of Primary Forest biomass that the 20-year prediction reaches
df_ecoregions$tmf_pct20 <- (df_ecoregions$tmf_agbd20 / df_ecoregions$pri_median) * 100

## Calculate the estimated time it would take to reach Primary Forest biomass, assuming continual linear regrowth
df_ecoregions$tmf_timetopri <- (df_ecoregions$pri_median - df_ecoregions$tmf_int) / df_ecoregions$tmf_slope
```

Lastly, we sort & save to report!
```{r sortandsave}
df_ecoregions <- df_ecoregions[order(df_ecoregions$tmf_timetopri),]
EcoregionReports <- df_ecoregions
usethis::use_data(EcoregionReports, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## The Output

The output is a data frame with 26 rows and 11 variables:

- **ECO_ID:** Unique numeric ID for each ecoregion, per the RESOLVE Ecoregions dataset
- **ECO_NAME:** Descriptive geographic name for each ecoregion
- **pri_n:** Count of points sampled within primary forests
- **pri_median:** Median aboveground biomass measured within primary forests, Mg/ha
- **tmf_n** Count of points sampled within regrowing forests, via the Tropical Moist Forests (TMF) dataset
- **tmf_slope:** Slope/growth rate of median aboveground biomass per regrowth age, via TMF regrowth years, Mg/ha/yr
- **tmf_int:** Intercept of the linear regression equation of median aboveground biomass per TMF age, Mg/ha
- **tmf_r2:** R^2 coefficient of determination from the linear regression equation of biomass/age
- **tmf_agbd20:** Predicted aboveground biomass after 20 years of regrowth, via the regression model, Mg/ha
- **tmf_pct20:** Percent that the 20-year biomass reaches compared to primary forest biomass, %
- **tmf_timetopri:** Estimated time needed for biomass to reach primary forest levels under linear regrowth, years
